Five distinct VERY TALL playable structures, each 50-80 metres tall, lots of actual stacked floors, generous hollow walkable spaces, visible internal stairs and flat landings, flush climbable faces without projecting trim. Orthographic three-quarter architectural game concept render. Landscape comparison board with five equally sized separate vertical panels on neutral pale blue, all towers complete from feet to top. Left to right: '01 Sky Tree': a tapering 72m Y-shaped tower built from six huge stacked 4-floor rigid cassettes, three broad radial spine walls, recessed floors and open sky courts between wings. '02 Zipper Spire': 60m stack of large counterbalanced folded Z-shaped 3-floor sections, alternating mirrored cantilevers and diagonal stair streets through the middle, centered broad bearing spine, not a loose leaning pile. '03 Spiral Lantern': tall hollow cylindrical lantern made from stacked chunky open cage sections containing two broad opposing spiral ramps with frequent flat landings; enormous central atrium visible. '04 Cross-Block Relay': six 4-floor inhabited box-girder bars, long horizontal volumes stacked alternately X then Z at their central broad bearing patches, building rises 72m like giant interlaced Jenga bridges, large hollow corridors and rooftop streets. '05 Cage Cathedral': three gigantic open octagonal structural cage sections, each contains multiple exposed floors and broad internal stairs, few huge diagonal ribs integral to each cage; section seams and removable bright gold bearing shoes visible. Do not use miniature regular buildings. Inventive but physically coherent toy structures.
